ranges.note: Vol. I No. 1, 1833-11-26 — the only Democrat printed in November 1833 and the first number of the paper. Read through, 33 claims. Declared as the calendar month because that is the seam T-0258 was split on (T-0308..T-0315, one month each); the month holds one issue and the range therefore asserts exactly that one. THE SCAN RECORD IS SENIOR HERE and six claims carry `reading: scan_verified` where data/sources/chicago_democrat_1833_11_26.json read type the transcription could not, or read it differently. NO POST-OFFICE LETTER LIST in this issue — swept for every form the Democrat uses, for no hit — so ruling 1 is met by demonstrating absence, as T-0261 met it for the American. The transcription is deposit-held, so the quotes were machine-checked with `--check --deposit <path>` against a read-only copy of the deposit from `main`; on `dev` their claims are counted unresolved and reported, which is green (T-0275).

Vol. I Nos. 2-6, 1833-12-03 to 1833-12-31. Five issues, read through. Their transcriptions are deposit-held, so the quotes were machine-checked with `--check --deposit <path>` against a read-only copy of the deposit from `main`; on `dev` their claims are counted unresolved and reported, which is green (T-0275). THE MONTH CARRIES NO POST-OFFICE LETTER LIST. Swept all five issues for every form the Democrat uses — 'list of letters', 'letters remaining', 'remaining in the post office', 'uncalled for', a signature ending 'P. M.', and the bare words 'post office' and 'postmaster' — for hits in every issue and not one of them a list: they are the paper's OWN agent list on page 1, which names eight out-of-county postmasters (George Cloud of America, Elijah Willard of Jonesboro', Daniel Converse of Waterloo and so on) and is reprinted unchanged in all five numbers, plus two national paragraphs about the Post Master General (1833-12-17) and the Postmaster of New-York (1833-12-24), plus J. Bates jr.'s standing advertisement asking enquirers to call at the P. Office. The hand count the ticket asks for is therefore ZERO printed lists against ZERO extracted names, and it agrees with T-0308 next door: No. 1 of 1833-11-26 carries none either. The Chicago post office's own list does not appear in this corpus until 1 January 1834, printed cut on 1834-01-14 and nearly whole on 1834-01-28 (T-0310). THE MONTH'S PRINCIPAL DOCUMENT IS THE WHARFING ORDINANCE of 4 December 1833 — sections 11-16 adopted at the house of Dexter Graves, printed first on 1833-12-10 and legibly on 1833-12-24, minted once from the second, on T-0292's one-printing-one-claim discipline. THE DIALECT CHANGES INSIDE THE RANGE: Nos. 2-5 are dash-column and No. 6 is the prose `Newspaper Page` / `Column` pair, and No. 2 carries the BARE `SOURCE PDF PAGE n` banner, whose pages the resolver counts ordinally because the scan page is not the issue page (this issue opens at scan page 5). THE ORDINANCE WAS ALREADY IN THE CORPUS FROM ITS JANUARY REPRINT: T-0310 read sections 11, 13, 14 and 15 off 1834-01-07 before these December printings were read. Those claims stand; the December ones are kept beside them because they are the SENIOR witnesses — first printing on 1833-12-10, clearest on 1833-12-24 — and because each carries text the January reprint lost: the four names of the bridge committee and the word REPAIRING, the whole of the eighty-feet and fifteen-dollar clauses, the whole of section 16, and the president's and clerk's signatures. Each of the seven December ordinance claims names its January counterpart in its own notes.

Vol. I Nos. 7-10, 1834-01-07 to 1834-01-28. Four issues, read through. Their transcriptions are deposit-held, so the quotes were machine-checked with `--check --deposit <path>` against a read-only copy of the deposit from `main`; on `dev` their claims are counted unresolved and reported, which is green (T-0275). THE LETTER LIST: the post office at Chicago's list of 1 January 1834 is printed twice in the month — cut to a handful of names on 1834-01-14 and nearly whole on 1834-01-28 — and the residents are minted from the second, where 97 names and the postmaster's signature survive. Ninety-seven is a FLOOR and not the printed length: the .docx extraction crushed the list's two alphabetical columns into eight paragraph lines and left orphan debris where names stood. The gap is a ticket, not an estimate.

Vol. I Nos. 11-14, 1834-02-04 to 1834-02-25. Four issues, read through. Their transcriptions are deposit-held, so the quotes were machine-checked with `--check --deposit <path>` against a read-only copy of the deposit from `main`; on `dev` their claims are counted unresolved and reported, which is green (T-0275). THE MONTH'S LETTER LIST IS THE 1 JANUARY 1834 CHICAGO LIST IN ITS THIRD PRINTING, at 1834-02-04 page 4 column 2, and IT IS THE BEST WITNESS THE CORPUS HOLDS TO THAT LIST. It is NOT minted: T-0310 already minted 97 residents from the printing of 1834-01-28, and T-0292's rule for a list printed more than once — mint once, record the reprints — is the rule T-0299 exists because July 1834 broke. The reading is made in full in the claim's `normalized` field instead. THE COUNT, stated against the printing as the ticket asks: 71 names survive at name level in the first alphabetical column, A to H, Atkins to Harkness, with four further lines of that column reduced to debris, so the printed first column was about 75 names. T-0310 minted 97 from the WHOLE list; ~75 in the A-H half alone confirms that ninety-seven is a floor and not the printed length, which T-0310's note asserted and this pass measures. This printing also REFUTES T-0318's premise that 'the images are the only route' — it is in the ruled dialect, one name per line, and repairs the A-H half at the transcription: 'William Cr[…]' is William Criss. T-0323 carries that. A SECOND letter list runs in the same issue, from an out-of-county office signed by Thomas Calaher and not by J. S. C. Hogan; it is recorded and not minted, as T-0292 recorded the Hennepin and Plainfield lists. Swept all four issues for every form the Democrat uses — 'list of letters', 'letters remaining', 'remaining in the post office', 'uncalled for', a signature ending 'P. M.' — for these two lists and, at 1834-02-11, the postmaster's own mail timetable, which is extracted as `infrastructure`.

Vol. I Nos. 15-17, 1834-03-04 to 1834-03-25. THREE ISSUES, NOT FOUR, AND THE HOLE IS THE DEPOSIT'S NOT THE PAPER'S — or at least that is as far as the evidence goes. The transcription of 1834-03-18 says so on its own face, in the deposit's own words: 'No March 11 issue is supplied; the printed sequence resumes with March 18, No. 16.' The numbering agrees and is the stronger witness: 4 March is No. 15 and 18 March is No. 16, so no number was printed and skipped between them. Whether the Democrat missed a week or its printer numbered through an unissued one is NOT settled here; what is settled is that no fourth March issue is missing from this reading. The range is declared as the calendar month, per the seam T-0258 was split on, and it asserts exactly the three issues the month holds. THE MONTH CARRIES A CHICAGO POST-OFFICE LETTER LIST, AND IT IS ONE NO EARLIER SWEEP HAD FOUND. data/research/newspapers/README.md recorded that only four of T-0258's thirty issues carry a list — 1834-01-28, 1834-02-04, 1834-04-23 and 1834-04-30. 1834-03-04 is a fifth, on page 4, and the reason every text sweep missed it is that the segmenter cut the printed column down its middle and took the heading with it: 'List of L' stands at the head of page 4 column 2 and 'etters ... ost-Offiee at Chica- ... 34.' at the head of column 3, so no search for 'list of letters' or 'remaining in the post office' could ever match. It is minted once, as two claims — c026 and c027 of 1834-03-04 — one per crop. THE HAND COUNT the ticket requires, made by eye off the printed list as this transcription preserves it: eighteen names in the first crop and sixty-one in the second, of which one is the postmaster's signature — SEVENTY-EIGHT PERSONAL NAMES EXTRACTED AGAINST SEVENTY-EIGHT COUNTED, plus John S. C. Hogan. That is a FLOOR and not the printed length: the Vision reading of both crops failed outright, the Tesseract fallback interleaved the names with whatever advertisement shared the printed column, every name has lost its left edge, and orphan debris stands where names stood. WHICH RETURN IT IS, SETTLED (T-0331): this is the CHICAGO POST OFFICE'S 1 JANUARY 1834 RETURN, printed for the ninth time. It stands in every Democrat from Vol. I No. 7 of 1834-01-07 to No. 15 of 1834-03-04, nine weeks unbroken, and four of those printings set the date line whole or nearly — 'go, Ill. January [1,] 1834.' at No. 7 — of which the '34.' at the head of this page's column 3 is the tail. The 1 March quarterly return floated here is refuted: a letter list is standing type and this is the last impression of one, not a second cohort, so T-0299's rule that one list mints once binds these names TOGETHER WITH January's. The sweep count above is superseded with it — nine Chicago printings stand in T-0258's thirty issues where the README recorded four, because the sweep searched for the heading and four of the nine headings are cut, illegible or in another crop. TWENTY-FIVE of the fifty-seven cut forenames are repaired from the concordant printings by `tools/letter_list_printings.py`; the remaining thirty-two are left cut with the tool's reason against each. NO PAGE IMAGE WAS READ and the claims stay `transcription_mediated`. The extracted 78 remains a FLOOR for the printed length: names the other printings carry and this crop does not — Anderson, Abbott, Austin, Axtell, Bertrand, Barrows, Bowen, Bradford, Britton at No. 7 line 645 alone — show the loss, and the printed length itself still wants the page images (T-0424). THE OTHER TWO ISSUES CARRY NO LIST: swept 1834-03-18 and 1834-03-25 for every form the Democrat uses — 'list of letters', 'letters remaining', 'remaining in the post office', 'uncalled for', a signature ending 'P. M.' — and also, because this month proved the headings can be cut in half, for the bare fragments 'ist of L', 'etters', 'ost-Off' and 'advertis'. The only hits are each issue's Arrivals and Departures of the Mails over J. S. C. Hogan's signature, extracted as `infrastructure`, and out-of-county postmasters in a Buffalo house's reference list. Their transcriptions are deposit-held, so the quotes were machine-checked with `--check --deposit <path>` against a read-only copy of the deposit from `main`; on `dev` their claims are counted unresolved and reported, which is green (T-0275).

Vol. I Nos. 18-22, 1834-04-01 to 1834-04-30. Five issues, read through, 71 claims. Their transcriptions are deposit-held, so the quotes were machine-checked with `--check --deposit <path>` against a read-only copy of the deposit from `main`; on `dev` their claims are counted unresolved and reported, which is green (T-0275). THE MONTH'S LETTER LIST IS THE 1 APRIL 1834 CHICAGO LIST, AND NOBODY KNEW IT WAS THERE. `data/research/newspapers/README.md` said in as many words that of T-0258's thirty issues only 1834-01-28, 1834-02-04, 1834-04-23 and 1834-04-30 carry a list, and T-0313's own brief repeated it as 'TWO letter lists (1834-04-23 and 1834-04-30)'. Both are wrong twice over. The two April lists that sweep found are the HENNEPIN list, printed three times in this month (1834-04-16 page 3 column 4, 1834-04-23 page 3 column 5, 1834-04-30 page 3 column 5) and recorded here without minting a name, as T-0290 and T-0292 treated the Hennepin and Plainfield lists before it. Chicago's own list of letters remaining on 1 April 1834, over J. S. C. Hogan's signature, is printed THREE times in the issues the sweep passed over — 1834-04-01 page 3 columns 3 and 4, again 1834-04-08 page 3 columns 3 and 4, and a third time at 1834-04-16 page 4 columns 2 and 3, which this note said was TWICE until T-0321 opened page 4 of No. 20 on 2026-08-29. The third printing was missed for the same two reasons as the others and one of its own: its heading is cut across two segmenter columns as `List el` / `EMAINIG in 1` and `ef Letters FFIC`; and 1834-04-16's own reading pass never opened page 4 at all, because all eight of that page's segmenter columns carry the Tesseract fallback banner. The HENNEPIN list this month's sweep did find at 1834-04-16 is on page 3 column 4 — a different list on a different page, and both stand. WHY EVERY SWEEP MISSED IT: the heading on 1834-04-01 reads `SQA AINIG init`, which is REMAINING, and the words `List of Letters` stand in the NEXT segmenter column over the list's second half; so a search for 'list of letters', 'letters remaining', 'remaining in the post office', 'uncalled for' or a signature ending 'P. M.' finds the Hennepin list in this month and not the Chicago one. It is minted ONCE (T-0292's rule, T-0299's complaint), from 1834-04-01: 163 names there, plus 16 names from the 1834-04-08 reprint that the first printing's transcription crushed, plus 12 more from the 1834-04-16 printing that neither earlier one held — 191 in one cohort, and nothing else from either reprint. THE THIRD PRINTING IS THE BEST WITNESS TO THE J-W HALF: it sets one name per line with no interleaved editorial and no debris line at all, it settles 1834-04-01's seven lost lines 3039-3045 as holding the five names 1834-04-08 supplied and nothing more, and it undoes a conflation — the list prints TWO Walkers, and 1834-04-01 c002 had minted one of them wearing the other's initials. 191 IS STILL A FLOOR AND NOT THE PRINTED LENGTH, and THREE positions are unread after all three printings: 1834-04-01's line 2869 (`is Bet i`), which has no counterpart in either reprint — both run Thos. W. Bradley straight into Lewis Benton — so whether a name stood there is not known; its line 2921 (`Jeter Porter ae`), debris in all three (`Jeter oats`, `tl. Jaiee pried Pet`); and a position between James S. Cook and Leander Collins that no ticket had named and that is legible in none of the three (`? Cook` at 1834-04-01 line 2901, `p, Cock` at 1834-04-16 line 3835). Every other debris line T-0321 names is closed: of its eleven at page 3 column 3, nine now carry a name (2881 and 2882 hold FOUR — Harriet Bradford, Eli Benn, Stephen R. Briggs and the previously unminted Robert Cook); and all seven at page 3 column 4, the block 3039-3045, are accounted for by the third printing's clean reading, which shows five names there and nothing else. Two forenames the third printing supplies for names 1834-04-08 could only mint by surname — Duncklo and Denny — are READ AND NOT MINTED, because joining them to the surname-only entries is the identity-policy question T-0392 carries and it is the owner's. The page-image pass that would close the rest is T-0321's standing ask. The month also carries what a reconstruction can actually use: the Board of Trustees' order of 5 March 1834 for a ten-foot plank or brick sidewalk with two-inch oak curbing along South Water Street, made at the house of Dexter Graves; John H. Kinzie's ware house opposite Fort Dearborn; a boot and shoe shop next door to P. Cohen's store; a dwelling house on lot 3 of block 18 and a store room in the rear of J. B. Beaubien's store house; and, on 1834-04-16, the sentence `Seven or eight buildings have been raised in this town within the past week`. TRANSCRIPTION QUALITY IS THE WORST IN THE RANGE SO FAR: 75 of the month's 160 segmenter columns carry the Tesseract fallback banner and they are concentrated on pages 3 and 4, where the town is.

Vol. I Nos. 23-26, 1834-05-07 to 1834-05-28. Four issues, read through. Their transcriptions are deposit-held, so the quotes were machine-checked with `--check --deposit <path>` against a read-only copy of the deposit from `main`; on `dev` their claims are counted unresolved and reported, which is green (T-0275). THE MONTH CARRIES NO POST-OFFICE LETTER LIST, which is what T-0314's own measurement table predicted (letter lists: 0) and this pass confirms by reading rather than by trusting it: all four issues were swept for every form the Democrat uses — 'list of letters', 'letters remaining', 'remaining in the post office', 'uncalled for', a signature ending 'P. M.' — for exactly two hits, and neither is a list. They are a reprinted debate mentioning the Post Master General (1834-05-07 page 4 column 8) and a Washington report naming the Postmaster-General (1834-05-14 page 2 column 6). The broader sweep for the bare words 'letter', 'list' and 'post office' returns forty-odd hits across the month and every one is a private letter quoted in news matter, a MARINE LIST, a probate 'letters of administration', or the standing 'letter press' line of a printing advertisement. So the hand count the ticket asks for is a count of ZERO printed lists against zero extracted, and the epic's letter-list ruling has nothing to bite on in May 1834. AGREES WITH ITS NEIGHBOURS in the way the corpus now expects: the Chicago office's 1 January return was printed twice in January (T-0310) and the next Chicago list this corpus holds is the 1 October one (T-0292), with September (T-0291) and August (T-0290) carrying none either.

Vol. I Nos. 27-30, 1834-06-04 to 1834-06-25. Four issues, read through, 73 claims. Their transcriptions are deposit-held, so the quotes were machine-checked with `--check --deposit <path>` against a read-only copy of the deposit from `main`; on `dev` their claims are counted unresolved and reported, which is green (T-0275). THE MONTH CARRIES NO POST-OFFICE LETTER LIST, and the sweep that says so was a READING and not a search — T-0313 proved a keyword sweep cannot find one on this deposit, because the heading of the 1 April 1834 Chicago list is set `SQA AINIG init`. So all ninety-six segmenter columns of the four issues were opened and read down, and every one of them is accounted for by subject: poetry and reprinted fiction, foreign news, the Bank controversy, the Illinois-Michigan boundary argument, the weekly price current, the marine list, and the advertising of pages 3 and 4. Not one carries a list of names, Chicago's or any other office's — the Hennepin list that runs through April, August and October is absent in June too. The hand count the ticket asks for is therefore ZERO printed lists against ZERO extracted names. That agrees with the two neighbours already read: T-0289 found none in July 1834 and the town's own 1 April list, minted by T-0313, had stopped printing after 1834-04-08. THE MONTH'S PRINCIPAL DOCUMENTS are the three town ordinances adopted at the house of E. Haddock on 6 June 1834 (the assessor's roll, the street supervisor's charge over every street, alley, road and bridge within one mile of the centre, and three days' labour a year owed by every male resident of twenty-one to sixty on pain of seventy-five cents a day) and the Democrat's own count of the building boom on 18 June: 'upwards of seventy-five buildings' put up since spring commenced, some of three storeys, two or three three-storey stores begun, a settled population of at least 1500, and lots on the principal street renting at $300 a foot front. THE PLACEMENTS: Clark, Filer & Co.'s cabinet ware house five doors east of the corner of Randolph on South Water; P. F. Peck at the corner of LaSalle and South Water; Kinzie & Hall one door east of the corner of Lake and Canal; Miss Waite's school on Randolph in a building nearly in rear of the Presbyterian Church between Clark and Dearborn; a large dwelling house and well on lot 7 of block 16, one lot east of Haddock's Tavern on Lake street; a sixteen-by-thirty-foot house on the corner of LaSalle and Lake at $250; Philo Carpenter at the sign of the Golden Mortar on South Water; Dally & Youngs's new blacksmith shop opposite the jail, erected the week it advertised. THE DIALECT IS RULED AND UNIFORM across all four issues, 96 column markers, every column carrying the Tesseract fallback banner. INTERLEAVING IS THE MONTH'S CHIEF DIFFICULTY and it is uneven: 1834-06-18's page 3 is not interleaved and is the witness the other three lean on, while 1834-06-11 is interleaved throughout and 1834-06-25's page 3 columns 3-6 are the worst text in the range. Where a bracketed supply comes from another printing of the same advertisement, the claim's notes name that printing.

Vol. I Nos. 31-35, 1834-07-02 to 1834-07-30. Five issues, read through. Their transcriptions are deposit-held, so the quotes were machine-checked with `--check --deposit <path>` against a read-only copy of the deposit from `main`; on `dev` their claims are counted unresolved and reported, which is green (T-0275).

NO CHICAGO POST-OFFICE LETTER LIST STANDS ANYWHERE IN THE MONTH: the town's 1 July return was withdrawn after 1834-07-16 and does not return, and the only list printed in August is the Hennepin one of 1 July, in its fifth week, cut across two segmenter columns of 1834-08-06 (claims c010 and c011 there) and extracted in full from the lines those columns carry. Swept all four issues for every form the Democrat uses — 'list of letters', 'letters remaining', 'remaining in the post office', 'uncalled for', a signature ending 'P. M.' — for four hits: the Hennepin list and its postmaster's signature in 1834-08-06, and the three out-of-county postmasters named in the paper's own agent list on 1834-08-20 and 1834-08-27. Their transcriptions are deposit-held, so the quotes were machine-checked with `--check --deposit <path>` against a read-only copy of the deposit from `main`; on `dev` their claims are counted unresolved and reported, which is green (T-0275).

Vol. I Nos. 40-43, 1834-09-03 to 1834-09-24. Four issues, read through. Their transcriptions are deposit-held, so the quotes were machine-checked with `--check --deposit <path>` against a read-only copy of the deposit from `main`; on `dev` their claims are counted unresolved and reported, which is green (T-0275). THE MONTH CARRIES NO POST-OFFICE LETTER LIST: swept all four issues for every form the Democrat uses — 'list of letters', 'letters remaining', 'remaining in the post office', 'uncalled for', a signature ending 'P. M.', and the bare words 'letter', 'postmaster' and 'list' — for no hit that is one. The four hits the broad sweep returns are a reprint of Senator Ewing's Post Office report (1834-09-24 page 3 column 1 line 2717), a Cumberland postmaster's letter about mail robbers (1834-09-10 page 3 column 1 lines 2382-2393), the Postmaster General's own Chicago-to-Green-Bay proposals (1834-09-17 page 3 column 3 lines 2807-2822, extracted as `infrastructure`) and a want-advertisement routing replies through the post office (1834-09-03 page 3 column 3 lines 3109-3118). The survey T-0291 was written against is therefore confirmed by reading rather than trusted: the epic's letter-list ruling has nothing to bite on in September 1834, and the hand count the ticket asks for is a count of zero printed lists against zero extracted. AGREES WITH T-0290 next door: August 1834 carries no Chicago list either, the town's 1 July return having been withdrawn in mid-July.

Vol. I Nos. 44-48, 1834-10-01 to 1834-10-29. Five issues, read through. Their transcriptions are deposit-held, so the quotes were machine-checked with `--check --deposit <path>` against a read-only copy of the deposit from `main`; on `dev` their claims are counted unresolved and reported, which is green (T-0275). THE MONTH'S LETTER LIST IS THE 1 OCTOBER 1834 CHICAGO LIST and it is printed three times — 1834-10-08 page 3 columns 1-2, 1834-10-15 page 3 columns 2-3, and 1834-10-22 page 1 columns 1-2. It is minted ONCE, from 1834-10-22, which is the only witness that carries it whole; the other two printings are recorded as reprints with their names unminted, so one list makes one cohort of people (T-0299). 1834-10-01 and 1834-10-29 carry no Chicago list — the latter prints the Hennepin and Plainfield ones, which are recorded and not minted, as are the Du Page and Plainfield lists under the Chicago one on 1834-10-22.

Vol. I Nos. 49-52, 1834-11-05 to 1834-11-26. Four issues, read through. Their transcriptions are deposit-held, so the quotes were machine-checked with `--check --deposit <path>` against a read-only copy of the deposit from `main`; on `dev` their claims are counted unresolved and reported, which is green (T-0275). THE MONTH CARRIES NO CHICAGO POST-OFFICE LETTER LIST. Swept all four issues for every form the Democrat uses — 'list of letters', 'letters remaining', 'remaining in the post office', 'uncalled for', a signature ending 'P. M.', and the bare words 'letter', 'postmaster' and 'post office' — for hits in one issue only, 1834-11-05, where THREE OUT-OF-COUNTY LISTS stand on page 3 columns 3-4, each dated 1 October 1834 and each signed by its own postmaster: Thomas Galaher's, C. Van Horn's and G. W. Laird's. None is Chicago's. Tested by names and not by signature alone: of the 149 names minted from the Chicago list of 1 October 1834 (T-0292, from 1834-10-22), NOT ONE matches Glen, Griffin, Grege, Hall, Hunt, Isaacs, Akin, Terry, Wier, Webb, Sawyer, Spangle, Twaddle or Shepherd, all of which stand in these columns — a zero overlap that no reprint of the same list could produce. So the survey T-0293 was written against is confirmed as to the matter ('October-list matter once more in No 49') and corrected as to whose list it is, the lists are recorded unminted (1834-11-05 c014), and the hand count the ticket asks for is a count of ZERO printed Chicago lists against ZERO extracted. AGREES WITH T-0291 AND T-0290 next door: the town's 1 July return was withdrawn in mid-July 1834 and the next Chicago list the corpus has is 1 October's, minted once from 1834-10-22. EVERY COLUMN OF PAGE 3 IN THREE OF THE FOUR ISSUES IS THE TESSERACT FALLBACK, cut at the left edge, with two physical columns alternating line by line; 1834-11-12 page 3 column 2 is the month's one Vision-set town column and is the witness the other issues' readings are checked against. AMENDED 2026-08-29, after T-0328 (PR #510): one claim added to 1834-11-26, c010 — the EARLIEST of five printings of D. Weaver's standing notice of a building for sale or to let on Lot 2, block 1, North Water street. This read passed over it, and that is worth recording rather than quietly repairing: the notice stands on page 3 column 3, which is one of the alternating pair this note already describes, so it survives as every other line and the word `Water` is lost to the column woven through it. Its absence is why the December read could not settle the lot number against 1834-12-17's `Lot 9`. The same shape of miss is worth looking for in the other three issues of this month. AMENDED AGAIN 2026-08-29, by T-0350, AND THE MISS THIS NOTE ASKED TO BE LOOKED FOR WAS THERE: two more claims are added, 1834-11-12 c015 and 1834-11-19 c012, both further printings of the same D. Weaver notice. The note above said “the same shape of miss is worth looking for in the other three issues of this month”; it was looked for, in the plainest way available — the whole run searched for the notice's own body text rather than for its advertiser — and two of the three issues were carrying it. That makes SEVEN printings of this advertisement in the corpus, not five, running unbroken from Vol. I No. 50 to Vol. II No. 4. WHY A NAME SEARCH COULD NOT FIND THEM, which is the transferable part: 1834-11-12 sets the signature “D. WEAVE.R”, and the surviving span of 1834-11-19 prints no name at all because the line that carries it is cut by the alternating column. A standing advertisement is best hunted by its body text, and the body text of a notice already claimed elsewhere is free evidence. THE SAME SEARCH IS WORTH RUNNING FOR EVERY OTHER STANDING NOTICE THIS MONTH'S ISSUES CARRY; it has not been, and this note does not claim it has.

Vol. II Nos. 1-4, 1834-12-03 to 1834-12-24. Four issues, read through, 56 claims. THE DEPOSIT IS ON THIS BRANCH AND EVERY QUOTE IS MACHINE-CHECKED ON `dev` ITSELF — the first Democrat month for which that is true. T-0275's back-merge landed the newspaper deposit on dev before this run started, so all four transcriptions resolve at their canonical chicago/reference/... paths with the sha256 corpus.json records, and none of the 56 claims is counted unresolved. Earlier months (T-0289 through T-0313) had to be checked with `--check --deposit <path>` against a copy from `main`. THE MONTH CARRIES NO POST-OFFICE LETTER LIST OF ANY OFFICE, and the hand count the ticket asks for is therefore ZERO printed lists against ZERO extracted names. Two independent instruments were used rather than one, because the keyword sweep alone is what T-0313 caught missing Chicago's own list of 1 April 1834: (1) all four issues swept for every form the Democrat uses — 'list of letters', 'letters remaining', 'remaining in the post office', 'uncalled for', a signature ending 'P. M.', and the bare words 'post office' and 'postmaster' — for hits in every issue and not one of them a list. Two of the seven are postmasters of OTHER offices, so those lists are reprinted ones and ruling 1 would not mint their names as Chicago residents in any case.

WHAT THE RANGE ADDS TO THE TOWN. Six public houses (the Sauganash newly refitted; the Exchange Coffee House at the corner of Lake and Franklin; the Eagle Coffee House, Trowbridge's, in or about Dearborn Street; the Tremont House on Dearborn Street; the New-York House on Lake Street; and the LAKE HOUSE still BUILDING in Kinzie's Addition on 1835-06-10, which is the only dated statement of its state anywhere in this corpus). Hubbard & Co's BRICK store in La Salle Street, the only wall material the papers state. Four weekly CHICAGO PRICES CURRENT tables whose building-materials block — lumber, shingles, square timber, brick at $5-6 the thousand, stone, lime, wood — does not move a cent in five weeks while superfine flour goes from $5.00-6.50 to $15.00-16.00. Fort Dearborn's own supply contracts: a year's fresh beef beginning 1 July 1835, five hundred cords of white oak, hickory, white ash and maple with the cord dimensioned, and twenty tons of prairie hay to be cut in July. Two editorials on the state of the streets and the standing water in the vacant lots, a town meeting in the Presbyterian church that answers them, and the same editor stating on 1835-06-24 that Chicago is 'uncommonly healthy' while cholera runs at Alton and Springfield.

WHERE IT IS THIN AND WHY. 1835-06-24's page 3 is a strict line-by-line interleave of the advertising with the federal land-sale proclamation, so several advertisements survive only as every other line of themselves: a Lake Street boot and shoe manufactory and a South Water Street auction house are placed and described but their proprietors' names fall on lines the interleave gave to the proclamation, and that issue's prices current is read only where label and figure both survive. 1835-05-27 and 1835-06-04's editorial columns are clipped at the line starts throughout. None of it is filled in.

Vol. II Nos. 16-18 (the printed number 18 repeats on 26 August), 1835-08-05 to 1835-08-26. Four issues, read through — the Democrat's last month in the corpus. Their transcriptions are the derived ones committed under text/, so every quote is machine-checked on `dev` itself and none of this month's claims is unresolved. THE POST-OFFICE LETTER LIST IS DECLARED READ AT PRINTING LEVEL AND NOT AT NAME LEVEL, AND THAT IS THE ONE THING THIS RANGE DOES NOT ASSERT. All four issues carry ONE list — letters remaining in the Post Office at Chicago on the 31st day of July 1835, over J. S. C. Hogan's signature — set once and printed unchanged four times; the heading is legible only in the 26 August printing and the name lists of the four are identical name for name and in the same order. Its heading and the postmaster are claimed in every issue that prints them (1835-08-05 c027, 08-12 c014, 08-19 c019, 08-26 c008) and its roughly six hundred names are NOT minted here: T-0299 measured that minting a standing list once per printing turned 298 names into 638 persons in the 1834 read. T-0336 owns the name-level extraction and will make it from one named printing. T-0297 was split for exactly this reason, on the same ground its own parent T-0260 was split — a six-hundred-name list is a run on its own and does not belong in a batch where it would be hurried. The month's standing advertising is claimed ONCE, from the 5 August issue, and is not re-claimed from the three later printings where it stands unchanged; the town ordinances passed 5 August 1835 run in three issues and are claimed from the 19 August printing, the only one a quote can be built from line by line. Each issue's own note names what it defers and what it refuses. Two traps are named and deliberately NOT claimed as Chicago's: the 'DESTRUCTIVE FIRE' of 19 August, which stands under a Cleveland Whig credit and carries the word Cleveland inside it, and the 26 August stage accident, which the paper credits to the Michigan City Gazette.
